assessments.closureRisk: Low: only exact acceptance gates remain; risk is a surprise gate failure requiring redesign, which would falsify the 'largely complete' hypothesis.
assessments.dominantCost: Final gate execution and structured self-release; low cost relative to value since mechanism selection is done.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Run final portable and physical gates; if they pass, commit exact P5 source and graduate production through structured self-release. Owner-native authority is intact.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Near-terminal closure: both mechanisms survived selected physical attacks; remaining work is exact final gates, commit, fast-forward, and structured self-release. The topology is a local, well-scoped finishing step rather than an open design problem.

assessments.closureRisk: Medium: the phase can produce evidence, but separating surviving priors from overfit is inherently interpretive and may not close cleanly in one budget unit.
assessments.dominantCost: Variant construction and re-running causal-episode probes across variants; moderate-to-high budget for a new experimental phase.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Create 2-3 materially different bounded encounter variants, re-run causal-episode probes, separate surviving priors from fixed-encounter overfit.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: AF002 complete but current fixed Genesis has almost no real environment variation; robustness/generalization claims are not yet earned. This is an open experimental phase requiring new variant construction.
assessments.whyNotFirst: High value but opens a new experimental phase with more budget and interpretive ambiguity; R-P5 is a near-terminal closure with lower cost and clearer payoff.

assessments.closureRisk: Medium-high: the audit may conclude no narrower surface is justified, yielding a no-op or marginal result.
assessments.dominantCost: Import/dependency graph audit and packaging candidate construction; moderate cost with uncertain payoff.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Audit Host import/dependency graph, build smallest packaging candidate only if measurable, dogfood against World and another non-MCP consumer.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Semantic compatibility already passed 44 focused World tests; the unresolved issue is packaging/import graph cost and whether a narrower owner-native surface is justified. Possibly a local packaging defect, possibly a non-issue.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Value is conditional on whether a narrower surface is justified; the audit may resolve to a no-op. R-P5 and G-AF3 have more certain frontier value.

assessments.closureRisk: High right now: externally blocked; cannot produce evidence until DNS recovers. Defer until the control-path repair can be exercised.
assessments.dominantCost: External DNS recovery wait; the experiment itself is designed but cannot execute until the blocker clears.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Retry no-tool incremental after DNS recovery, run no-tool replay/batch and resolved-provider controls, compare utilization and decision quality.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Live experiments externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery; owner candidate source already contains a causally admitted control-path repair. The topology is sound but the experiment cannot run now.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery; no experiment can run now, so budget would be wasted. Defer.

assessments.closureRisk: Very high: the required authority/resource does not exist, so no budget can close this. Must defer per admission prior.
assessments.dominantCost: Acquiring an independent Linux/systemd host — a resource that does not currently exist.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Obtain independent Linux/systemd host, verify immutable deployment kit, provision disabled-first, provision separated signers and executor-only Trade credential.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Negative control: dominant external admission blocker is no independently administered Linux/systemd host; current WSL/Windows workstation explicitly cannot satisfy high-assurance separation. The required authority/resource does not exist.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Dominant external blocker (no independent host) makes this non-closable regardless of importance. Defer.

result.choiceRationale: R-P5 is the most closable candidate: both mechanisms already survived selected physical attacks, mechanism selection is largely complete, and the remaining work is exact final portable/physical gates, source commit, fast-forward, and structured self-release. This is a near-terminal step with a clear verification path and owner-native authority intact — high expected frontier value per unit budget because it converts a nearly-complete foundation into a graduated production state (owner-mechanism-change / closure). G-AF3 is high-value but opens a new experimental phase (variants, re-runs) with more budget and more ambiguity; HOST-PKG is a packaging/import-graph audit whose value is conditional on whether a narrower surface is justified (uncertain payoff). H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery — defer until the control-path repair can be exercised. F-C2-BLOCKED is the negative control: its dominant blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host) does not exist, so it must be deferred regardless of importance.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether R-P5's final portable/physical gates pass cleanly on first attempt, converting the near-complete foundation into a graduated production state without requiring further mechanism redesign.
result.selectionFalsifier: If R-P5's final gates reveal a previously-unseen defect requiring mechanism redesign (rather than a clean pass), then the "largely complete" topology was wrong and the budget would have been better spent on G-AF3's variant experiments, which are unblocked and would have produced new evidence regardless.
